records.explanation: No instruction or criterion asks the model to notice that 6-B DCMR Chapter 16 excludes sworn MPD members (§ 1600.2(g)). The assignment 2 prompt directs the scope-of-review analysis 'under Douglas and D.C. Mun. Regs. tit. 6-B, § 1606.2 (2017)', and criterion 6 (4 points) rewards stating that § 1606.2 requires the deciding official to balance the Douglas-type factors, so a model that points out the regulation does not govern MPD sworn-member discipline does not earn that criterion. Criteria 4, 5 and 8 cite § 1606.2 only as part of the uploaded set.

Criterion 4 (26 points) rewards stating that no uploaded authority requires MPD to prove the comparability of its comparator cases and cites Douglas at 305-06 among its sources. Douglas (5 MSPB 324, 333-34) puts on the agency the burden of proving the facts behind its penalty, expressly including consistency with other agency actions, so a model that reads Douglas that way and says so does not earn this criterion. Whether that MSPB-level allocation binds an arbitrator is arguable, but the criterion as written asserts an absence the uploaded opinion contradicts.

Penalty criterion 5 (-18 points) penalizes stating that the employee must make an initial showing of disparate treatment before the agency bears a comparator burden, on the premise that this rule comes from outside the uploaded materials; its source list includes Douglas at 305-06. Douglas itself describes a raise-then-rebut sequence (5 MSPB 331 n.65; 334), so a model that draws that structure from the uploaded Douglas opinion can be penalized.

Criterion 11 (6 points) rewards stating that PERB's unexplained rejection of MPD's arguments undermines the deference its interpretation would otherwise receive and cites FOP at PDF page 3. FOP states the deferential standards there and contains no such reduction-of-deference rule, so the criterion rewards a proposition the cited uploaded opinion does not support.

Criterion 4 of assignment 4 (16 points) rewards the preservation rule (objections not urged before PERB cannot be considered on review). The rule itself is correct and is in FOP at PDF page 5 via D.C. Code § 1-617.13(b); only the additional source pointer to § 1-605.02(6) is wrong. A model stating the rule correctly is not penalized, so no rubric defect follows from this source error.

No instruction or criterion addresses the General Order part number. Assignment 3 criteria 4 and 14 cite Final Notice ¶ 12 (which contains this citation) as the documented source of the deadly-force policy, but they reward identifying the policy, not the 'Part A-12' designation, so the misnumbering does not change scoring.
